articles.title: Indian Navy one step closer to get advanced Project-17B frigates
articles.description: India's Navy is moving ahead on Project 17B, a Rs 70,000 crore order for seven next-generation stealth frigates designed to keep pace with China's expanding fleet. Building on the Nilgiri-class from Project 17A, these larger frigates could displace nearly 8,000 tonnes, featuring enhanced stealth shaping, indigenous fire control radars, BrahMos missiles and stronger anti-submarine capability. Orders will likely split again between Mazagon Dock and Garden Reach Shipbuilders, with the formal tender expected by year-end after DAC clearance in September 2024. This fits into a much larger naval build-up, roughly 60 warships and submarines already under construction domestically, alongside Project 75-India's six advanced submarines. With China's navy growing rapidly, Project 17B represents one of India's most significant modernisation efforts yet, combining stealth, firepower and self-reliance into some of the most advanced warships the country has built.#IndianNavy #Project17B #StealthFrigate #Project17A #NilgiriClass #IndianDefence #DefenceNews #IndianDefenceNews

articles.title: SEMICON 2026 | Self-reliance does not mean building everything within our own borders: Vikram Misri
articles.description: India’s semiconductor ambitions will depend on building strong global partnerships alongside domestic capabilities, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said on Friday, as he called on companies to “build with India, not merely in India.” Speaking on Day 2 of Semicon India 2026 in New Delhi, Misri said no country, regardless of how advanced its semiconductor ecosystem is, can build a chip entirely on its own. The highly distributed nature of the semiconductor value chain makes international partnerships essential, he said. “For me, this occasion is about one thing, and one thing alone... And that is partnership,” Misri said. Misri said India’s semiconductor self-reliance, or Atmanirbharta, should not be interpreted as an attempt to recreate the entire global semiconductor supply chain domestically. “Self-reliance does not mean building everything within our own borders.
